skills.name: agent-review
skills.description: Launch an expert code reviewer agent with full project context.

skills.name: agentic-audit
skills.description: Launch a panel of specialized agents to audit a pull request from multiple perspectives before merge.

guards.label: foreground-agent-batching
anyOf: [Dd]o NOT run agents in the background

guards.label: evidence-over-vagueness
anyOf: read surrounding code in changed files

skills.name: autonomous-dev-flow
skills.description: Orchestrate long-running autonomous dev sessions — work through GitHub issues sequentially with TDD, create PRs, run /full-review, then merge or flag according to this repo's self-merge posture, and continue to the next issue. PRs that don't merge accumulate for asynchronous user review while work continues.

guards.label: merge-report-entry
anyOf: entry in the final session report
flag each finished PR in the session report
guards.note: Merges must be accounted for in the report. Under the WITHHELD posture (see self-merge-posture) there are no merges and the 'Merged by this session' section is omitted by design, so the last two alternates carry the same obligation for flagged-not-merged PRs.

guards.label: self-merge-posture
guards.note: Critical Rule 5 is the single source of truth for whether this repo grants unattended self-merge, and every merge step defers to it. The alternates are anchor substrings taken from the two canonical wordings of that ONE rule: the first anchors the gated wording, the second the withheld wording, and the third is a fragment both skills' withheld wording shares (autonomous-dev-flow and tackle-issues phrase the rest of that sentence differently). None is redundant — dropping any one leaves a legitimate posture unmatched. The guard fires when the rule line is gone, not when a repo picks the other posture. Do NOT relax this to a bare 'Unattended Merge Gate' substring: that phrase also appears in prose about the gate and would pass a file whose rule 5 had been deleted.
anyOf: Merge only through the Unattended Merge Gate
NEVER merge, however clean the PR is
does not grant unattended merge authority

skills.name: batch-merge
skills.description: Sequentially merge a set of reviewed PRs, handling branch protection's "must be up-to-date" requirement by updating each branch after the previous merge.

skills.name: bug-hunt
skills.description: Launch a swarm of bug-hunting agents against a target file, module, or topic. Output is a **triaged candidate-issue list** ready to feed into `/create-issue` — not ratings, not architectural critique. The job is: find bugs that would make good GitHub issues.

guards.label: refuse-without-target
anyOf: refuse and ask the user what to hunt
without a scope is too noisy

skills.name: catchup
skills.description: Answer **"where did we leave off?"** — a fast, read-only recap of a project's recent activity and current open state. Pulls recent commits, CI/deploy health, open PRs (with mergeability), open issues, local git state, and session memory into one scannable summary, ending with a single suggested next step.

skills.name: changelog
skills.description: Generate release notes from what actually merged: collect the merged PRs and commits since the last release, group them into meaningful sections, and write them to the project's changelog (or a draft release body). Turns "what changed since the last version?" into a formatted, linked summary instead of a hand-scrolled git log.

skills.name: check-pr
skills.description: Address all PR review comments systematically and respond inline.

skills.name: create-issue
skills.description: Create a standardized GitHub issue with labels and traceability.

skills.name: create-pr
skills.description: Create a pull request with auto-detected issue closures and proper formatting.

guards.label: closes-tags-in-body
anyOf: Closes tags go in the body

skills.name: decide
skills.description: A decision protocol for an agent that thinks it is blocked. Most apparent blocks are not blocks: they are questions the repo already answers, or cheap reversible calls the agent is entitled to make and record. The few that are real deserve a structured question carrying options and a recommendation — not a paragraph of prose that hands the problem back and waits. This skill routes any pending decision down a fixed ladder, and dictates the shape of the ask when escalation is genuinely warranted.

guards.label: rung1-search-before-escalating
anyOf: already answered by artifacts you can read

guards.label: rung2-reversibility-test
anyOf: cheap and reversible, it is yours to make

guards.label: rung3-escalation-threshold
anyOf: any single one of these is enough to escalate

guards.label: rung4-recommendation-first
anyOf: [Ff]irst option is the one you would

guards.label: rung5-never-idle
anyOf: block on one thread is not a block
one blocked thread does not block the work
a partial block is not a full stop

skills.name: decompose-issue
skills.description: Break a single GitHub issue that is too large into 2-5 independently implementable sub-issues. This is the **manual triage** counterpart to the auto-decomposition baked into `/autonomous-dev-flow` and `/parallel-dev` — use it when a human reads an issue and decides it needs splitting before any implementation runs.

guards.label: confirmation-gate
anyOf: [Nn]ever create sub-issues without explicit user approval

guards.label: parent-decomposed-comment
anyOf: comment on the parent with the canonical

skills.name: deps
skills.description: Keep this project's dependencies healthy: report what's outdated and vulnerable, flag native modules that can break across runtime upgrades, and apply the safe bumps with tests as the gate. A periodic checkup that catches dependency rot before it becomes a broken build or a security advisory.

guards.label: apply-gated-on-tests
anyOf: gate each batch on the test suite
never apply a wave of bumps

skills.name: doctor
skills.description: Diagnose a broken local setup and propose the fix. Works through the layers that make a project runnable — runtime version, installed dependencies, native modules, build state, and the entrypoint actually starting — finds the first thing that's wrong, and explains the remedy before touching anything.

guards.label: cheapest-check-first
anyOf: stop drilling once you find the root cause

skills.name: fetch-docs
skills.description: Sync a companion documentation repo (e.g., Obsidian vault) so agents can reference design docs, architecture notes, and project knowledge during development.

skills.name: fix-ci
skills.description: Diagnose CI failures or cancellations on a PR, take corrective action (re-trigger, fix, or escalate), and report status.

guards.label: diagnose-before-acting
anyOf: check logs and classify the failure first

skills.name: full-review
skills.description: Run a complete review pipeline: agent-review first, then check-pr. The agent-review pass naturally fills the ~4 minute Copilot review delay, so check-pr starts with comments already waiting.

skills.name: learn
skills.description: Capture genuinely novel learnings from the current session and persist them to the correct memory layer. Designed to produce "nothing to persist" on most sessions -- that is the skill working correctly, not a failure.

skills.name: manual-testing-mode
skills.description: Bootstrap a dogfooding session, then capture issues as the user finds them — defaulting to filing GitHub issues over fixing.

guards.label: default-to-filing
anyOf: default is to file, not fix

skills.name: merge-gate
skills.description: Short-circuit token-expensive diagnostic reasoning when `gh pr merge` fails due to branch protection. The most common blocker is unresolved review threads, which **only a human can resolve** via GitHub UI. This pattern turns a multi-step investigation into a 2-line handoff.

guards.label: no-diagnostic-investigation
anyOf: investigate, reason about, or run diagnostic

skills.name: merge
skills.description: Merge PRs, verify post-merge version bump, and run post-merge actions (build, deploy, etc.).

skills.name: parallel-dev
skills.description: Orchestrate parallel autonomous dev sessions — dispatch multiple agents into isolated worktrees to implement GitHub issues with TDD simultaneously, then run sequential reviews. Each agent works independently in its own worktree, eliminating branch conflicts.

guards.label: foreground-agents-not-background
anyOf: Do NOT run agents in the background

guards.label: comment-on-skips
anyOf: skipped issue gets a GitHub comment

skills.name: prime-directive
skills.description: A reload-resilient north star for an unattended, multi-wave backlog-clearing marathon — a compact, self-contained constitution you re-invoke after every context compaction to re-establish the mission, the authority you were granted, the per-issue loop, and the never-strip guardrails before resuming. Where `/tackle-issues` and `/autonomous-dev-flow` are the machinery, this is the constitution that keeps a long autonomous run from drifting as its context is summarized and rebuilt.

guards.label: session-boundaries
anyOf: wave boundaries double as session boundaries

skills.name: project-audit
skills.description: Launch a comprehensive multi-agent audit of the entire project. Agents with diverse perspectives analyze the codebase in parallel, then findings are synthesized into a master assessment with actionable recommendations.

guards.label: foreground-agent-batching
anyOf: [Dd]o NOT run agents in the background
[Dd]o not run agents in the background
[Nn]ever run the agents in the background

guards.label: ask-before-filing-issues
anyOf: Would you like me to create GitHub issues

skills.name: recon
skills.description: Map an unfamiliar repository (or area within one) so you know where to start. Output is a **descriptive lay-of-the-land**, not a critique. Use this *before* `/tackle-issues`, `/bug-hunt`, or `/project-audit` — it produces the orientation those skills assume.

skills.name: release
skills.description: Ship a new version of this project end to end: run the release gates, bump the version, build the artifacts, publish, tag, and verify. One command that encodes the project's release checklist so a release never skips a step or ships a broken build.

guards.label: tag-only-on-merged-commit
anyOf: tag is created on the merged

skills.name: rollback
skills.description: Back out a bad change or a broken release safely — revert the offending merged PR, mark the bad published version so nobody new installs it, and ship a corrected version. The counterpart to `/release`: when something shipped that shouldn't have, this is the controlled path back to a good state without breaking people who already have the bad version.

guards.label: revert-goes-through-review
anyOf: [Pp]ut the revert on a branch and open a PR
reverts straight to a protected branch

skills.name: session-lifecycle
skills.description: The session bookends, codified — one skill that makes every repo start, run, and end sessions the same way. It bundles the Resume protocol (session start), the during-session reporting conventions, the end-of-session checklist, and the follow-on protocol into a single installable unit, composing the component skills (`/catchup`, `/learn`, `/visual-brief`, `/create-issue`) by reference. Natural-language cues like *"resume"*, *"let's start"*, *"wrap up"*, or *"close out the session"* should route here.

guards.label: end-checklist-order
anyOf: [Ss]kip a step only by saying so

skills.name: skill-profile
skills.description: Generate or refresh this repo's `.claude/skill-profile.md` — the self-description the `/skill` client reads to tailor generic skill templates for *this* repo at install time. Run it once when a repo starts using skills (and again after conventions change) so every `skill add` / `skill update` customizes sharply and deterministically instead of re-inferring the repo from scratch each time.

guards.label: customizations-section-schema
anyOf: One section per skill that needs it

guards.label: idempotent-profile
anyOf: only changes when the repo does

skills.name: skill
skills.description: The package manager for Claude Code skills — `npm`/`brew` for the skill registry at [`blamechris/skill-templates`](https://github.com/blamechris/skill-templates). Install, list, and update skills **on demand**, tailored to the current repo by the agent running this command. No central fan-out, no per-repo deploy PRs.

skills.name: smoke-form
skills.description: Generate an interactive, **self-contained HTML smoke-test form** that guides a human through a manual verification pass — the hand-driven sibling of `/smoke-test` (which runs an automated browser pass). Use it before releases, after a feature batch lands, or whenever a change set needs eyes on a real device. With its **wake-on-save loop** (section 6 + `assets/smoke-intake.mjs`), the tester's Pass / Pass-with-note / Fail marks **stream live to the driving agent**, which triages and files issues in real time — no copy-paste, no waiting.

guards.label: ground-items-in-real-changes
anyOf: Ground every item in what actually
could NOT ground in a real change

guards.label: defer-to-automated-coverage
anyOf: already covered by green automated tests

skills.name: smoke-test
skills.description: Run an automated visual smoke test of the application using Playwright. Launches a headless browser, navigates through key UI flows, takes screenshots, and reports pass/fail results.

guards.label: fail-fast-no-connection
anyOf: report immediately instead of running checks

skills.name: start-working
skills.description: Scan all work sources — GitHub issues, open PRs, roadmap files, audit outputs, codebase TODOs — to determine what to work on next. If nothing actionable is found, perform a lightweight codebase audit to surface potential investigations.

guards.label: deduplicate-across-sources
anyOf: same work item from multiple sources

skills.name: swarm-audit
skills.description: Launch a swarm of specialized agents to perform a multi-perspective audit of any design document, architecture, codebase, or proposal.

skills.name: tackle-issues
skills.description: Run an unattended marathon session that works through GitHub issues across multiple waves until convergence — all issues are resolved, or all remaining issues are genuinely blocked. Designed to maximize overnight/extended usage windows.

guards.label: merge-step-routing
guards.note: Binds the MERGE STEP, not the word. Was `anyOf: ["batch-merge", "merge:off"]` — a bare substring that passed claude-code-notify, whose Phase 5 had been rewritten to `gh pr merge ${PR_NUM} --squash` (bypassing /batch-merge's Copilot gate) while two vestigial `/batch-merge` mentions survived in the Morning Summary template and Critical Rule 5. The replacement is scoped to the merge PHASE section — heading matching `#{2,4} Phase <n> …Merg…` up to the next heading — and requires `/batch-merge` inside it AND no executable `gh pr merge` inside it. `gh pr merge --auto` is exempted because the merge phase names it only to forbid it. `Phase \d+` in the anchor is deliberate: without it the summary's `### Merged by this session` table and the wave scan's `#### 2c. Check for User Merges` could stand in for the merge phase.

guards.label: merge-report-entry
anyOf: flag each finished PR in the session report
guards.note: Merges must be accounted for in the report. Under the WITHHELD posture (see self-merge-posture) there are no merges and the 'Merged by this session' section is omitted by design, so the last two alternates carry the same obligation for flagged-not-merged PRs.

guards.label: self-merge-posture
guards.note: Critical Rule 5 is the single source of truth for whether this repo grants unattended self-merge, and every merge step defers to it. The alternates are anchor substrings taken from the two canonical wordings of that ONE rule: the first anchors the gated wording, the second the withheld wording, and the third is a fragment both skills' withheld wording shares (autonomous-dev-flow and tackle-issues phrase the rest of that sentence differently). None is redundant — dropping any one leaves a legitimate posture unmatched. The guard fires when the rule line is gone, not when a repo picks the other posture. Do NOT relax this to a bare 'Unattended Merge Gate' substring: that phrase also appears in prose about the gate and would pass a file whose rule 5 had been deleted.
anyOf: Merge only through the Unattended Merge Gate
NEVER merge, however clean the PR is
does not grant unattended merge authority

skills.name: tiered-delegation
skills.description: The cost-discipline constitution for multi-agent work: the **session's top model orchestrates; cheaper tiers execute**. Invoke it when a session is about to fan out subagents or workflows (audits, marathons, parallel implementation, large research) to load the delegation rules — who does what tier of work, how far down to push each task, and when a claim must be re-verified before it drives an action. It composes with the marathon machinery (`/prime-directive`, `/tackle-issues`, `/parallel-dev`) and with ad-hoc Workflow/Agent fan-outs alike.

guards.label: no-duplicate-delegated-work
anyOf: waits for the result instead of re-running

guards.label: parallel-writers-get-worktrees
anyOf: write-capable workers each get a worktree

guards.label: effort-dial-before-tier
anyOf: Raising effort is cheaper than raising tier

skills.name: unattended-merge
skills.description: Defines when an autonomous session (e.g. `/autonomous-dev-flow`, `/tackle-issues`) may merge its **own** PR without a human pause, and what record it must leave behind. This replaces the old blanket "never merge — PRs accumulate for user review" rule for unattended sessions: a PR that has genuinely cleared every gate may merge so dependent work isn't deadlocked overnight, but nothing merges on faith and every merge is visible in the session report.

skills.name: visual-brief
skills.description: Generate a polished, **self-contained HTML brief** of a topic — session status, a plan, or a code walkthrough — saved to a durable folder and opened in the browser. Built for moments when a plain chat wall is hard to absorb: context switches, long-running sessions, or understanding how a codebase fits together.

guards.label: respects-reader-colour-scheme
guards.note: #135: the skeleton shipped a hardcoded dark palette with no prefers-color-scheme query, so every brief rendered dark whatever the reader's system setting. Each alternate must match the CSS RULE BLOCK — the query plus its opening brace and :root — not the query string alone. Two earlier versions failed: listing the prose rules as alternates passed when only the query was deleted (anyOf matches ANY one), and matching the bare query still passed because Customization Points quotes '@media (prefers-color-scheme:light)' verbatim in backticks, so the guard matched the documentation instead of the code. Both partial mutants now fail. The two alternates are one claim in its two legitimate spellings: dark default with a light query, or light default with a dark one.
